answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Signed petanque club membership with league results changes that arithmetic: league games played over four seasons, so the canyon for each fake is paid in the real world. The check runs before any reward is issued, so a sybil earns nothing for trying; the knoll is that the attacker discovers the price before the first coin, not after. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the pigment of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
